Prepare spatial covariates for native unmarked prediction

Source: R/prepare_unmarked_data.R
prepare_unmarked_data.Rd

Calculate the optimized spatial predictors at new sites and insert them into an explicitly keyed data frame for native unmarked prediction. The training means and standard deviations are reused, so the new sites are on the fitted model's covariate scale. Pass the result to unmarked::predict(), or give the same inputs to prepare_prediction() for a reusable snapshot.

Usage

prepare_unmarked_data(
  object,
  newdata,
  kernel_inputs,
  join_by,
  include_fixed = FALSE
)

Arguments

object

A fitted multiScaleR object whose opt_mod is an unmarkedFit, with its fitted scales, training standardization, and retained kernel_inputs.

newdata

A nonempty data frame of prediction rows, in the layout that native unmarked prediction needs for your chosen component. Include the site key columns and every non-spatial variable, including factors and offset inputs. Existing optimized spatial columns are replaced. Supply fixed-radius predictors on their fitted scale unless include_fixed = TRUE. Other columns and the row order are left unchanged.

kernel_inputs

A multiScaleR_data object from kernel_prep() for the new sites. Use the fitted kernel, source and metric definitions, buffer extent (max_D), raster resolution, and the same binned or exact evaluation as the fit. Landscape and surface metrics need cell-level inputs, while lean binned inputs are enough for kernel means.

join_by

A data frame with one unique key row per prepared site, in kernel_inputs point order. Its column names must occur in newdata, and every newdata row must match a key. Repeated keys in newdata repeat that site's spatial values, which lets you write site-by-year or site-by-survey scenarios without changing their order. Required.

include_fixed

Logical. The default FALSE leaves fixed-radius predictors as native inputs that you supply. Set TRUE to calculate modeled fixed-radius metrics at the new sites too, after verifying that their retained preparation values and standardization match the fitted static site covariates. Missing or inconsistent training information raises an error.

Value

A data frame with the same rows, row names, and non-spatial columns as newdata. The calculated spatial columns hold the fitted kernel transforms in standard-deviation units of the training sample, the scale the native model was fitted on. They are model inputs, not predictions. Do not standardize them again.

What the function does and does not do

This function prepares data only. Native prediction determines the component's meaning, factor handling, offsets, missing-data behavior, and confidence limits, and neither this function nor prepare_prediction() adds uncertainty in the selected scales. multiScaleR-prediction lists what each unmarked component predicts.

Spatial predictors are static site covariates, as the unmarked fitting adapter requires. Supply the native row layout for detection and annual components yourself. The function does not infer observation times, expand sites into years, modify an unmarkedFrame, or borrow non-spatial values from the fitting data.

Match the spatial inputs to the fit

Distances inside kernel_inputs are converted with its own unit_conv, and the reported scales remain in map units. Metric definitions and the choice of binned or exact kernel evaluation must match the fit. Preparing bins at new sites can shift their representative distances slightly, as in other binned prediction routes. Source names are checked, but raster contents are not fingerprinted, so prepare the sites from the intended source rasters and coordinate system. When the internal fitted parameters are retained, they are reused directly, which avoids rounding from a conversion to reported units and back. Stored parameters that disagree with the reported scales or shapes raise an error.

The calculated columns use the training sample's mean and standard deviation. Prediction values are never clamped or standardized within the new sample. Missing spatial values stay missing for the native prediction method, while infinite values or invalid training standard deviations raise errors.

Recompute fixed-radius predictors

Fixed-radius predictors are recalculated only with include_fixed = TRUE. Their normalization comes from the original preparation object, and their fitted site values must match that object after explicit training-site alignment. This rejects manually rescaled or stale fixed predictors, changed radii, ambiguous training keys, and missing training buffers rather than guessing their fitted scale. Keep the original inputs if you need this verification.

Distance-removal models

For unmarked::gdistremoval() fits, only active component formulas identify spatial predictors. Availability is inactive with one primary period, and the distance formula is inactive for a uniform key. Optimized static site names must not also occur in the native yearly or observation covariate tables, so use distinct names for distinct inputs. Dot formulas use the original component's available training-column names. GDR models with active formula offsets or TMB zero inflation are rejected, as aic_tab() explains.

See also

prepare_prediction(), predict.multiScaleR(), multiScaleR-prediction, kernel_prep(), kernel_scale.raster(), and vignette("v02-user-guide", package = "multiScaleR") for fitting and mapping unmarked models.

Examples

## A stored N-mixture fit used in vignette("v02-user-guide"). Abundance
## depends on the bin1 and cont2 layers of a simulated landscape.
nmix <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "cache-user-guide-nmix.rds",
                            package = "multiScaleR"))
layers <- subset(sim_rast(user_seed = 999, dim = 250), c("bin1", "cont2"))

## Three new sites, prepared with the fitted kernel, max_D, covariate
## definitions, and binning
new_pts <- terra::vect(cbind(x = c(800, 1250, 1700),
                             y = c(900, 1250, 1600)))
new_inputs <- kernel_prep(new_pts, layers, max_D = nmix$max_D,
                          kernel = nmix$kernel_inputs$kernel,
                          scale_vars = nmix$kernel_inputs$scale_vars,
                          bin = !is.null(nmix$kernel_inputs$binned),
                          verbose = FALSE)

## Keys follow the prepared point order. Site B appears twice, for
## example in two survey years, and reuses the same spatial values.
keys <- data.frame(site = c("A", "B", "C"))
scenarios <- data.frame(site = c("A", "B", "B", "C"))
nd <- prepare_unmarked_data(nmix, scenarios, new_inputs, join_by = keys)
nd  # bin1 and cont2 in training standard-deviation units
#>   site       bin1     cont2
#> 1    A  0.8463096 0.9121894
#> 2    B  1.6378884 0.6597968
#> 3    B  1.6378884 0.6597968
#> 4    C -1.1986195 0.6290868

## Expected abundance at each row, with native 95% confidence limits
unmarked::predict(nmix$opt_mod, type = "state", newdata = nd)
#>   Predicted        SE     lower     upper
#> 1 2.2541203 0.3245970 1.6998190 2.9891759
#> 2 4.6758934 0.6758364 3.5223707 6.2071771
#> 3 4.6758934 0.6758364 3.5223707 6.2071771
#> 4 0.7324141 0.1144437 0.5392024 0.9948591

## The same rows and component as a reusable snapshot
prepared <- prepare_prediction(nmix, scenarios, new_inputs,
                               component = "state", join_by = keys)
predict(prepared)
#>   Predicted        SE     lower     upper
#> 1 2.2541203 0.3245970 1.6998190 2.9891759
#> 2 4.6758934 0.6758364 3.5223707 6.2071771
#> 3 4.6758934 0.6758364 3.5223707 6.2071771
#> 4 0.7324141 0.1144437 0.5392024 0.9948591
